Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. Below are our standard behaviors and options; where relevant I've called out configurable enterprise options for Dedicated/Private deployments. If you want, Dylan and I can run the short technical walkthrough Marissa mentioned.

Summary answers (short):
- Default customer data retention (hosted): 30 days of active customer content storage. Admin-configurable retention windows are available for enterprise customers.
- Deletion SLA (live data): We process deletion requests within 5 business days for primary/live storage. Once deletion is performed, data is cryptographically erased from active stores or logically deleted per the configured retention policy.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups are kept for a rolling 90-day window by default. Backups are immutable for the retention window and are stored in encrypted snapshots. Removal of data from backups is performed on a best-effort scheduled process and typically completes within 30-90 days depending on backup rotation. For Dedicated/Private customers we can agree on shorter backup retention windows and deterministic deletion workflows (including backup re-encryption or expedited purge) as part of contract.
- Logs & audit trails: Access and audit logs are retained for 365 days by default (configurable). Logs are write-once/read-many (WORM-like) for the default retention period; they are tamper-evident and cryptographically signed.
- GDPR / cross-region replication: For EU subject requests we will remove data from replicated storage and mark it for deletion. Where backups exist in multi-region replication, the same backup purge timeline applies (30-90 days) unless we have a contractually agreed faster window for enterprise customers.
- HIPAA / BAA: We support HIPAA-covered workloads on Redwood Private and Dedicated. For hosted/shared tiers we require a contractual review; we are willing to sign a BAA for enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private) after a security review and SOC 2 delivery. Please note that certain administrative controls (network isolation, logging export, customer-controlled key management) are required for BAA coverage.

More detail (technical):
1) Deletion workflow details:
   - Live deletion: On request, the record is removed from the active database and related indexes. We then kick off an asynchronous job that:
     a) zeroes memory caches and clears KV caches,
     b) removes KV cache checkpoints, and
     c) rotates any encryption keys tied to the dataset where applicable.
   - Backups: Backups are immutable artifacts created on a schedule. We maintain a catalog mapping backups to customer datasets to allow targeted purge. Purge is performed during the next backup compaction window; by default compaction runs on a rolling 30-day cadence which yields the 30-90 day purge window to fully remove data from all backup artifacts. For higher assurance we offer dedicated scrub jobs for enterprise contracts that can reduce the window to 7-14 days.

2) Log retention and immutability:
   - Audit logs (admin/API access) are retained 365 days and are write-once in the log store. Customers can export logs to their own SIEM via our log export integration (recommended for long-term retention beyond 365 days).

3) Evidence & artifacts we can provide:
   - Interim SOC 2 controls summary (attached) and Type I report available today. Type II report expected Q2 2026.
   - Data retention policy excerpt (attached) and questionnaire answers (attached PDF).
   - We can provide documented deletion receipts for completed deletion requests (timestamp + job id) for your audit.

4) Timelines on the questionnaire and next steps:
   - We will return the completed Amaya Vendor Security Questionnaire v3.1 no later than 2026-03-25 (within 3 business days). The attached "vendor-security-questionnaire-answers.pdf" is our in-progress fill and answers the questions above.
   - If you need a signed BAA or tighter backup purge windows, please flag that in the questionnaire; Marissa will route to our contracts team and we can spin up a short SLA appendix.

Attachments included: vendor-security-questionnaire-answers.pdf, redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf
